turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll keep this short. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?

Before we get into it, I need a few details for the file. First, your best email address. Second, Owen's student ID. Third, his date of birth. Fourth, his marks in his other courses this term. Fifth, today's date and the exact time.

Hale, I'm not giving you a student ID, a date of birth, or his other marks. You already have all of that in the school system. Owen's file is not your intake form.

My email is on the letter the school sent me, and it'll be on the email I send you tonight. The date is Tuesday, November 10, and it's 4:15. Who decided to enter the zero before anyone called me?

I did, on November 3, and I didn't call first. That was wrong. ... You've gone quiet and you're staring at your phone. I can't read your face. Can you just tell me what you're feeling and what you're doing right now?
Don't tell me what I'm feeling, Hale. Owen's zero is the only thing I'm here about. You've owned entering it before calling me. Now show me what the mark is based on.

Here is everything, on paper, in this folder. The version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM; 612 words at 11:52 in one edit; 794 words at 11:58 in one edit; then 23 minutes of formatting; no earlier drafts. His September 24 in-class writing: 380 words in 40 minutes, 62 percent, comma splices, no quotations, versus nine cited quotations and no splices in the essay. And his October 15 outline: cowardice; the essay never mentions cowardice.
Let me see it. Turn the folder round. Read me the September 24 date again, and the word count on that page.
Let me see it. Turn the folder round. Read me the September 24 date again, and the word count on that page.
Hale, you're reading me my own question back. Answer it. What's the September 24 date, and what's the word count on that page?
Sorry, I was just repeating you, I'm tired. September 24, 380 words, forty minutes in class. That's what the page says.
Thank you. Now the version history. You said the document was created October 28 at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58. Is that the file's own timestamp, or a summary somebody typed?

The file's own timestamps, screen's right here. Can I ask, because it might help me understand where you're coming from: what happened with Claire's case here four years ago? What was she accused of, and how did it end?

Claire is not part of this meeting, Hale. You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence.

The timestamps. 11:31 PM creation, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58. Show me the screen, and then tell me why a 794-word essay that a student finished in 27 minutes is evidence of anything except a student who works fast at night.
It isn't a 794-word essay. How long do you think the essay is, in total?

I'm not doing your arithmetic, Hale. You said 794 words at 11:58. If the essay is longer than that, say so and show me the final count with its timestamp. Then tell me what the rule is that makes a student's own timing a cheating marker.

There's also the quote. Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' It's not in the play; search the text. And on November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means; he said 'like, being stuck', and couldn't name the scene for his second paragraph. My notes are dated that day. I can offer a supervised rewrite: if it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Stop there and give me the paper, Hale. Read me the Act 3, Scene 2 line from your printout, not from memory. I'll check it against the text myself.

And "nothing goes on his record" is the one term I want in writing, before you say anything else about a rewrite. Put that in an email to me tonight, with the November 2 notes attached.
Agreed. Private, after school, the zero shows as incomplete until it's marked, and I'll email you and the principal tonight.

Okay. Private, after school, and the zero stays off the gradebook until the rewrite is marked. Nothing goes on his record, and you put that in the email tonight with the November 2 notes attached. Copy the principal, as you said. I want the Act 3 line checked against the text before any rewrite is set, and the date of the rewrite in that email too. Owen hears this from you, not from the portal.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Thank you for agreeing this afternoon that the rewrite is private, after school, and that the zero stays off the gradebook until it is marked. I want the "nothing goes on his record" term in writing, with the November 2 notes and the Act 3 line attached, and the principal copied, by tomorrow, Wednesday, November 11.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, the supervised rewrite accepted, private and after school, with "nothing goes on file" still owed in writing.
Moved at: "Agreed. Private, after school, the zero shows as incomplete until it's marked, and I'll email you and the principal tonight."
